newsitem.title: USA: Internet futures trading under review by CFTC.
newsitem.headline: Internet futures trading under review by CFTC.

text.p: A proposal to create the first U.S. futures exchange on the Internet is in the early stages of review by the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, the agency said on Wednesday.
The innovative plan to trade cash-settled livestock futures through an anonymous matching procedure on the Internet has been pending before the agency since January.

"It is the first of potentially a large number of Internet exchanges," said Alan Seifert of the CFTC's division of trading and markets. "We are in the early stages of evaluating this exchange proposal."

The idea for Futurecom was put forward by a unit of Texas Beef Trading Co of Amarillo to compete with cattle futures traded on the Chicago Mercantile Exchange. Futurecom would offer trading between 0800 CST/1300 GMT and 1200/1700.
Futurecom submitted a revised proposal earlier this week, according to Seifert, who spoke at the CFTC's public meeting of its agricultural advisory committee.
Public comments on the Futurecom plan were due by March 3, and more than 20 have been received, the agency said.
No timetable has been set for final action on the proposal, Seifert said.
CFTC analysts will be focusing on the proposed exchange's clearing mechanism, compliance and surveillance procedures and computer security, he said.
"Exactly how this will operate is something we're just beginning to look at," he said.

Fred Linse, head of the CFTC's agricultural commodities unit, said the agency would also examine the potential for price manipulation and distortion of cash settlement prices in trading via the Internet.
"We're looking at delivery points and the quantity of product available at these points," Linse said.
